title: BN engine/client protocol 0.2
description: Application values of the JSON-RPC 2.0 methods and notifications. Framing is not described here. Sequence, revision and visibility invariants are checked by the engine and its reconstruction tests.

counter.description: Canonical decimal uint64 string, at most 18446744073709551615.

text.description: Player-facing text: a string, already localized for the connection, or a LocalisedString for the client to render from the engine's catalogues. 0.2 engines send strings only.

key.description: The msgid. The empty key concatenates `args`.

plural.description: The count that selects the plural form.

args.description: Values for the placeholders, in order.

dim.description: Game dimension_id; empty string is the primary dimension.

pos.description: Absolute map square. Never a reality-bubble coordinate.

name.description: Player-facing name the native look shows, translated: "wooden floor" for t_floor. Absent for creatures (the entity's name) and ids the data no longer knows.

tile.description: Tile id native tilesets look up when it differs from id: corpses (corpse_<monster>), characters (player_male, npc_female), vehicle parts (vp_<id>).

looks_like.description: The looks_like chain of the game data, nearest first, in the same namespace as the sprite id. A tiled client tries the sprite id, then these in order.

subtile.description: Multitile key the native tile selection chose from the known neighbours (terrain, furniture, trap, field) or the part state (vehicle part: open, broken, else center).

rotation.description: Quarter turns the native selection chose: 0 north, 1 west, 2 south, 3 east. Vehicle parts: the facing in four directions. Absent means 0.

facing.description: Side a creature faces; tilesets flip the sprite for left.

stack.description: Items on the square when there are several, on the displayed (last) item; the native view highlights such a stack.

tint.description: Paint of a vehicle part, or the tint of a field type (both layers alike). A tileset tints the part's background and foreground sprites with it (the native view blends hue and saturation toward it); a missing member is unpainted.

mutation.description: Set on the overlay of a mutation: its id, and its types and flags, which a tileset's tints and tint_pairs are keyed by to tint the overlay with the character's hair, skin or eye color.

tint_keys.description: The ids a tileset's tints are keyed by for this thing (flags, then the id), kept to the tint_ids the client sent in its hello, in the order the native view tries them.

tint_vars.description: The tint the own variables of an item, terrain or furniture square (tint_color, tint_blend_mode, ...) ask for, over what the tileset's tints give for the item.

kind.description: Left out when the cell layer already says it: terrain, furniture, trap, field, item and vehicle_part for the same-named layer, and memory.terrain as terrain.

name.description: Player-facing name the native look shows, translated: "wooden floor" for t_floor. Absent for creatures (the entity's name) and ids the data no longer knows.

tile.description: Tile id native tilesets look up when it differs from id: corpses (corpse_<monster>), characters (player_male, npc_female), vehicle parts (vp_<id>).

looks_like.description: The looks_like chain of the game data, nearest first, in the same namespace as the sprite id. A tiled client tries the sprite id, then these in order.

subtile.description: Multitile key the native tile selection chose from the known neighbours (terrain, furniture, trap, field) or the part state (vehicle part: open, broken, else center). Absent means center.

rotation.description: Quarter turns the native selection chose: 0 north, 1 west, 2 south, 3 east. Vehicle parts: the facing in four directions. Absent means 0.

facing.description: Side a creature faces; tilesets flip the sprite for left.

stack.description: Items on the square when there are several, on the displayed (last) item; the native view highlights such a stack.

tint.description: Paint of a vehicle part, or the tint of a field type (both layers alike). A tileset tints the part's background and foreground sprites with it (the native view blends hue and saturation toward it); a missing member is unpainted.

hides_items.description: The field's type hides the items under it: the native tiles view draws neither them nor their highlight while it is the displayed field.

light.description: Native lit_level of a visible square: 0 dark, 1 low, 2 bright only, 3 lit, 4 bright. Low light draws darkened.

below.description: A square in sight on the avatar's level that the native tiles view looks through (open air and other terrain without a floor, such as treetops, glass roofs and ramps down): how many levels down the square is that it draws here (the first square with a floor or with something remembered on it, when it is in sight, remembered or a vehicle; else the lowest square in sight with something on it on the way down). The square keeps what is on it, such as a field; bare open air carries nothing else, and bare open air with nothing seen through it is not published.

reviving.description: A corpse on the square can rise; the native view marks the square. Present only on visible squares.

cargo.description: A cargo part of a vehicle on the square holds items; the native view highlights the part. Present only on visible squares.

overlays.description: Sprites drawn over a character, bottom first, as looks of kind overlay: id is the overlay (worn_<item>, wielded_<item>, mutation_<id>, bionic or effect), tile and looks_like the tileset ids to try in the native order. A tileset without a sprite for an overlay draws nothing.

attitude.description: How the creature regards the avatar; the native view marks monsters and NPCs with an overlay of it.

aware.description: Present when the creature is aware of the avatar (its overlay says it sees the player).

traits.description: The ids of the character's mutations by mutation type (hair_color, skin_tone, ...): the colors a tileset tints its mutation overlays with.

id.description: Names the row for the pickup and drop operations. Stable while the stack stays what it is; two equal rows are told apart by their order.

count.description: How much the row holds in native units: charges of a charges item, else items. The most a pickup or drop of the row takes.

label.description: The row as the native lists word it: the display name of the stack with its count and condition marker as color markup, then the translated slot of a wielded or worn item.

short_label.description: The abbreviation the native sidebar prints before the value (Str), translated. Absent where it prints none.

compass.description: The monsters and NPCs the avatar sees alive within the loaded map and not on its own square, by the direction of their horizontal offset from it (center for the avatar's own column): what the native compass panel lists, clockwise from north and center last. Directions with none are absent. A client decides for itself which of them lie outside its own view.

overlays.description: Sprites drawn over a character, bottom first, as looks of kind overlay: id is the overlay (worn_<item>, wielded_<item>, mutation_<id>, bionic or effect), tile and looks_like the tileset ids to try in the native order. A tileset without a sprite for an overlay draws nothing.

traits.description: The ids of the character's mutations by mutation type (hair_color, skin_tone, ...): the colors a tileset tints its mutation overlays with.

short_label.description: The abbreviation the native sidebar prints before the value (Str), translated. Absent where it prints none.

compass.description: The monsters and NPCs the avatar sees alive within the loaded map and not on its own square, by the direction of their horizontal offset from it (center for the avatar's own column): what the native compass panel lists, clockwise from north and center last. Directions with none are absent. A client decides for itself which of them lie outside its own view.

overlays.description: Sprites drawn over a character, bottom first, as looks of kind overlay: id is the overlay (worn_<item>, wielded_<item>, mutation_<id>, bionic or effect), tile and looks_like the tileset ids to try in the native order. A tileset without a sprite for an overlay draws nothing.

traits.description: The ids of the character's mutations by mutation type (hair_color, skin_tone, ...): the colors a tileset tints its mutation overlays with.

keep.description: Members of the previous avatar that carry over unchanged.

avatar_update.description: An avatar in an event: the members named in keep equal the previous avatar's and are left out; every other member that is absent is empty.

label.description: The label the native panel prints before the value, translated. Absent where it prints none.

color.description: Native color name of the value where the color carries meaning. Absent otherwise.

sidebar_text.description: A value the native sidebar prints. A client lays it out and draws it itself.

mode_text.description: The native one-letter name of the mode (W), translated.

weather.description: Unlabelled underground, where the native panel prints only the underground text.

clock.description: The watch time, the approximate time of day without a watch, or the native unknown-time text underground.

sidebar.description: The values the native classic sidebar shows, with the labels its panels print. Limb health and stamina are numbers: a client lays the sidebar out and draws the bars itself.

season.description: Season of the calendar; tilesets name seasonal sprites with a _season_<name> suffix.

mod_tilesets.description: The files of the game data that add sprites to tilesets, in the order the native view loads them. A tiled client numbers their sprites after those of its tileset, for the files whose compatibility names it.

path.description: The JSON file, as the engine names it: relative to the game folder it runs from, unless absolute.

base.description: The folder the sheet files of the file are named from, named the same way.

index.description: Which mod_tileset of the file this is, counting from 1.

compatibility.description: The TILES names of the tilesets it adds sprites to.

hotkey.description: The key that chooses the row natively, printed before the label (a uilist entry's key, an inventory item's invlet). Absent when the row has none.

pane_id.description: The pane or tab this entry belongs to. Tab rows of a tabbed menu have none.

key.description: The stable, untranslated name of the column; clients look a column up by it, never by `label`.

color.description: The game color the native screen prints the value in. Absent when it uses the default.

favorite.description: The row is a favorite, as the native list marks it. Absent when it is not.

color.description: The game color of the row's text. Absent when the native list uses its default.

key_color.description: The game color of the row's `hotkey`. Absent when the native list uses its default.

markup.description: The row's name with the native color tags, when it differs from `label`.

action_id.description: The registered action the row runs, such as `open_options` on the in-game main menu. Absent on other rows.

parent_id.description: The listed row this one is nested under. Absent when it has no parent or the parent is filtered out.

nest_color.description: The game color of the nesting slash the native list draws before a nested row, lit by how much of its parent is marked. Absent for a row that is not nested.

mark.description: The selection mark the native list prints before the row: `+` all of it, `#` some of it, `-` none. Absent when the list prints none.

editor.description: A value the client can set directly with `fill` (field_id is this choice's id) instead of cycling it natively. `bool` takes `true` or `false`, `select` one of `values[].id`, `integer` and `float` a number within `minimum` and `maximum`, `text` a string of at most `max_length` (-1: unbounded). `value` is the current value in the same form.

page.description: The native page indicator of a paged list, counted from 1 (the NPC trade window).

blocked_areas.description: Registered actions of the areas the pane cannot put items in; the native screen draws them red.

distance.description: How far current is from source by distance_metric, as the game measures range (rounded Euclidean for trig, Chebyshev otherwise; the vertical axis included).

unit.description: Present when positions are overmap terrain squares (the overmap is open), not map squares.

status_text.description: Present where the screen reports range and readiness in words: the localized line, such as range 3/10, ready to fire.

parts.description: What the native look window prints of the cursor square, fact by fact. Present on the look-around screen; on a shot, the creature under the cursor.

vehicle.description: The native vehicle interaction window (veh_interact). `mode` select is the pick-a-part list of siphon, crew and the like. `cells` is the grid around the cursor in screen cells relative to it (x right, y down); `parts` are the parts on the cursor square, topmost first; `stats` are the native stat lines in reading order (an empty string is a blank slot). In a task list (install, repair, remove, mend, refill) the choices are the candidate parts, `tabs` is the install tab bar, and `detail` previews the highlighted part with its requirements. Choosing the highlighted part starts the task, choosing another part moves the highlight.

owned.description: The player owns the vehicle, so rename, crew and label are allowed.

verb.description: What the task does to the highlighted part, localized, such as `Install`. Absent on the main screen.

blocked.description: Terrain, furniture or a creature keeps the cursor square from taking a part.

color.description: A game color name such as `light_gray`.

name.description: The name with its contents or cargo load, as the native part list prints it.

open.description: The mark before the name: `[` for structure, `(` for armor, `-` otherwise.

tabs.description: The install tab bar. Choose `tab:<index>` to switch.

time.description: Absent when the pane has no time line.

time_heading.description: The localized heading of the time line; absent with `time`.

groups.description: The requirement headings in the order the native pane prints them.

empty_text.description: Printed under the heading when no requirement has this kind, such as NONE. Empty: leave the group out then.

text.description: A component or tool row lists its alternatives joined with OR.

can_do.description: Every requirement is met, so choosing the part starts the task.

overmap.description: Overmap squares as the player knows them, row-major. Each cell is [glyph, foreground, background] with curses color indexes 0-15 (0 black, 1 red, 2 green, 3 brown, 4 blue, 5 magenta, 6 cyan, 7 light gray, 8-15 their bright forms). Positions are overmap terrain squares.

cursor_description.description: What the native sidebar says of the cursor square, localized, without the window frame or the square's glyph.

cursor_here.description: `You are here.`, localized, when the cursor is on the player's square; absent otherwise.

cursor_note.description: `Note:`, localized, followed by the text the native window prints in its corner for the cursor square's note, such as `Note: cache`; absent when it prints none.

route_text.description: The length of the planned travel route as one localized line, such as `Route of 2 squares.`; absent without a route.

notes_title.description: The heading of the notes, localized: the name of the action that lists them.

labels.description: The names the native window prints over squares while its city-label toggle is on and the level is 0: the cities and labelled squares the player has seen, with the curses color indexes 0-15 the window prints them in. Absent when none.

mission_target.description: The square of the active mission's target while the overlays are shown; the native window marks it at its edge when it lies outside the window. Absent without a target.

path.description: The planned travel route, nearest square first.

tiles.description: Only for a client that said `tiles` in hello. `cells[row][col] = [tile, rotation, subtile]`: the overmap_terrain tile id, quarter turns and multitile key (empty for a plain tile). `looks_like` lists, per tile id, the ids to try next.

message_tone.description: Present where the native screen colors the message line, green for good and red for bad: the NPC trade balance.

category_mode.description: Present where the native screen has a category-selection mode: whether it is on (the NPC trade window).

any_key_choice_id.description: Present on a press-any-key screen that binds no key: the choice any key press acknowledges. Choose it when the player presses a key no action binds.

areas.description: The advanced inventory's area picker as the native header lays it out. `action_id` is the registered action that points the active pane at the area, `key` the key the player has bound to it (empty when none), `x` and `y` its position in character cells from the picker's top-left corner, `available` whether the area exists now (the vehicle is grabbed or on the square, the level is there). A pane is on the area whose `label` is its `area_label`.

refresh_ms.description: Present where the engine redraws the screen on its own every this many milliseconds with no input, such as the snake game; each redraw publishes a new screen.

interaction.description: choices holds at most the first 200 rows, fewer when they would be too large; read the rest with bn.interaction.choices from offset = choices.length. choice_total is the full count.

stack.description: The open screens, outermost first; the last is the one input goes to and the only one with affordances. Present on every boundary a 0.2 engine sends, next to the 0.1 `interaction`, which a screen's `root` replaces once its slice lands.

The open screens, outermost first; the last is the one input goes to and the only one with affordances. Present on every boundary a 0.2 engine sends, next to the 0.1 `interaction`, which a screen's `root` replaces once its slice lands.

interaction_update.description: A boundary in an event. `actions` is left out when it equals the previous boundary's; the client keeps its own.

screen_id.description: One native screen instance: stable while it stays open, new when it is reopened. The map's id is fixed for the epoch.

role.description: `map`: the running game. `dialog`: a question over it that the player answers and leaves. `screen`: a place of its own, such as a menu or a manager.

root.description: `null`: the screen is not described by components yet; read the boundary's `interaction`.

affordances.description: What the player can do on this screen; empty for a screen that input does not reach. Only the last entry of `stack` has any.

refresh_ms.description: Present where the engine redraws the screen on its own every this many milliseconds with no input, such as the snake game; each redraw publishes a new screen.

dock.description: Where the player asked a list window to sit, such as the pickup list. Absent when the screen has no such choice.

context.description: Diagnostics and tests only. Clients must not branch on it.

screen.description: One screen of the interaction stack.

view.description: The squares of the avatar's level a map click selects: the native terrain window, which follows the avatar.

changes.description: Applied in member order: coverage, view, cells, forgotten, entities, gone, then avatar/environment/route/interaction replace.

label.description: The line as the native log prints it: text, followed by the translated repeat suffix from a count of 2.

lang.description: Present when the line is not in the connection's locale: the BN language id it was rendered in.

data_message_logged.description: One line of the native message log. A repeat of the last line is published again with the same id and a higher count and replaces it.

direction.description: Where the native message says the sound comes from. Absent when the sound is at the avatar's square or the avatar sees its source, where the message names no direction.

distance.description: Squares between the avatar and the source, as the native sound code counts them.

turns.description: Whole turns left on a fuse: published when the fuse is lit and again every turn it burns.

tile.description: Tile id the native tiles draw the explosion with.

scroll.description: The unit step the text moves by each animation step.

kind.description: hp: a creature's hit-point readout, which stays beside it.

data_combat_text_shown.description: Floating text at a square, as the native scrolling combat text: one or two colored segments.

tiles.description: The client draws tiles, so the engine adds tile ids where it has them (the overmap).

tint_ids.description: The ids of the tints the client's tileset has (hair colors, item or terrain ids, flags). The engine publishes on looks the tint_keys among them that apply, in the order the native view tries them.

credits.description: Pushed `bn.events` and `bn.command` frames the engine may send before the client grants more with `bn.credit`.

max_hz.description: The most frames per second of wall time the engine publishes while an activity runs; the boundary where the activity ends is always published. Without it the engine paces only by its own cost.

delivery.description: Opt in to credit delivery. Without it every pushed frame is written at once, as before.

schema.description: Raw-byte SHA-256 prefix of 0.2.schema.json the client was built with. A mismatch fails with `negotiation_failed`; the engine never falls back to an older version.

locale.description: BN language id, such as `ko_KR`. Default: the engine's.

tiles.description: The client draws tiles, so the engine adds tile ids where it has them (the overmap).

tint_ids.description: The ids of the tints the client's tileset has (hair colors, item or terrain ids, flags). The engine publishes on looks the tint_keys among them that apply, in the order the native view tries them.

credits.description: Pushed `bn.events` and `bn.command` frames the engine may send before the client grants more with `bn.credit`.

max_hz.description: The most frames per second of wall time the engine publishes while an activity runs; the boundary where the activity ends is always published. Without it the engine paces only by its own cost.

delivery.description: Opt in to credit delivery. Without it every pushed frame is written at once, as before.

capabilities.description: What the client can do; the same members as the loose hello members, which stay accepted.
Either `capabilities` or the loose members, not both.

hello_params.description: A hello offers 0.2 and names the schema it was built with; any other version is refused with `negotiation_failed`.

tileset.description: The TILES option: the tileset the native client would load.

screen_queue.description: How many commands that wait for a screen (`expect.screen_id`) the engine holds behind the running one.

credits.description: The window granted, which is also the initial credit.

held_frames.description: At most this many pushed frames wait for credits.

held_bytes.description: At most this many bytes of pushed frames wait for credits.

max_hz.description: The frame rate cap the hello asked for; present exactly when it did.

delivery.description: Present exactly when the hello asked for credit delivery. Past either held bound the engine drops what is waiting and sends `bn.resync` with reason `backpressure`; `lost_after` is the newest sequence it wrote.

credits.description: Credits held after the grant, capped at 256; frames waiting for credits follow the response.

screen_id.description: The screen that must be on top of the stack; otherwise `stale_screen`.

affordance_id.description: An affordance of that screen with `holdable`; any other is `invalid_arguments`.

hold_params.description: The key of a holdable affordance went down. From now on, while the screen stays on top and waits for input, the engine takes one step of it at each input prompt, as if the native key were pressed once more, until `bn.release`. A client sends it once on key down, never for a key repeat. A hold replaces the previous one; a popup or any other screen on top, a step that changed nothing, a new `bn.hello` and a disconnect end it. Fails with `not_ready` while an activity runs.

view.description: The squares of the avatar's level a map click selects: the native terrain window, which follows the avatar.

messages.description: The newest message log lines, oldest first, as `message.logged` events carry them. Omitted when the log is empty. Applying the stream's `message.logged` events to this list (a repeat replaces the line with the same id; keep the newest 100) gives the list a later subscribe returns.

component_id.description: The `list` to read, when the screen has components. Absent: the 0.1 list of the interaction.

choices_result.description: With `component_id`: the rows of that list from `offset`, and its total. Without: the 0.1 choices.

error_text.description: Present with error: the localized reason, specific where the engine knows more than the kind.
Present with error: the localized reason, specific where the engine knows more than the kind.

schema.description: On a `negotiation_failed` that refused the hello's `schema`: the hash this engine was built with and the one the client sent.

route.description: The native auto-move route a map click planned and not yet confirmed: the squares to walk, nearest first, ending at the clicked square. Empty or absent when nothing is planned.

viewport.description: Map cells the client can show, as columns and rows of the native terrain window.

kind.description: What the fact is about. Parts come in the order the native look view prints them.

text.description: The fact, localized, with color tags.

detail.description: What more the view says of it when it has room, such as a creature's description; absent for none.

id.description: The identity of what the fact is about, such as a terrain id; absent for none.

values.description: Numbers the fact reports, by name, such as `move_cost`, `count`, `hp` and `max`.

tile_part.description: One fact the look and target views tell of a square or of the creature on it.

hotkey.description: The key that chooses the row natively, printed before the label (a uilist entry's key, an inventory item's invlet). Absent when the row has none.

key.description: The stable, untranslated name of the column; clients look a column up by it, never by `label`.

color.description: The game color the native screen prints the value in. Absent when it uses the default.

favorite.description: The row is a favorite, as the native list marks it. Absent when it is not.

color.description: The game color of the row's text. Absent when the native list uses its default.

key_color.description: The game color of the row's `hotkey`. Absent when the native list uses its default.

markup.description: The row's name with the native color tags, when it differs from `label`.

parent_id.description: The listed row this one is nested under. Absent when it has no parent or the parent is filtered out.

nest_color.description: The game color of the nesting slash the native list draws before a nested row, lit by how much of its parent is marked. Absent for a row that is not nested.

mark.description: The selection mark the native list prints before the row: `+` all of it, `#` some of it, `-` none. Absent when the list prints none.

max.description: The most a count for the row can be, in the row's native units (charges for a stack). Absent: the row takes no count.

header.description: A category heading over the rows after it, not an entry. Absent on an entry.

toggled.description: The row switches something on or off, and this is which it is now. Absent for a row that is no switch.

affordances.description: The row's availability for the affordances placed on its list where it differs from the row's own `enabled`/`denial`: a row that allows some of them only.

look.description: What the row stands for, for a client to draw. Absent for rows that are not things.

row.description: One row of a `list`. `id` is what an affordance's `row`/`rows` argument names. `enabled`/`denial` say whether the list's affordances apply to it.

One row id of that component: a `list` row, a `tabs` tab, a `grid` cell, a `form` field or a `map` target candidate. `avatar.ground` and `avatar.inventory` name the rows of the avatar's ground and inventory.

rows.description: Several rows of that list; with `counts`, each may carry a count.

count.description: A number within `min` and `max` where given.

text.description: A string for that form field. Without `field_id` the field is the one `row` names.

pos.description: An absolute position: a map square, or an overmap terrain square with `overmap`. With `component_id`, the square must lie inside the bounds and range of that `map` component's cursor.

pane.description: A pane (`panel`) id among the children of that component.

arg_shape.description: The arguments an invoke of the affordance must carry: every member present must be supplied, no other. An empty object means no arguments.

label.description: The native action name (`input_context::get_action_name`) or the screen's own word; never invented by the adapter.

keys.description: The player's bindings, as keybinding-file key names.

role.description: What the affordance means for the screen. `any_key` runs on a key no affordance binds. `select` moves the screen's cursor to the row named by `args.row` without activating it, so the detail that follows the cursor shows that row; a client invokes it when its focus moves in the list its `args.row` targets.

holdable.description: The affordance is a step of the map that the player can hold down: a client sends `bn.hold` when its key goes down and `bn.release` when it comes up, and does not invoke it for key repeats.

expect.description: Which expectation an invoke carries, assigned by the engine. `screen`: the affordance takes no `row`, `rows`, `pos` or `text`; the invoke expects `{screen_id}` and may queue. `boundary`: the invoke expects `{boundary_id, revision}` and the engine checks its row ids against the full list.

affordance.description: Something the player can do now, invoked by `id` with an `invoke` operation. Ids are opaque.

invoke_args.description: The members the affordance's `args` shape names, and no others.

item_id.description: The id of a row of avatar.ground (pickup) or avatar.inventory (drop).

count.description: How much of the row, in its native units: charges of a charges item, else items. At most the row's count.

invoke.description: Runs an affordance of the expected boundary. The engine checks `args` against the affordance's shape and rejects with `invalid_arguments` before running anything; an id the boundary does not offer is `unknown_affordance`.

oneOf.description: Holds while that screen is the top of the stack; otherwise `stale_screen`. For affordances with `expect: screen`.
Holds while the boundary and revision stand; otherwise `stale_boundary` or `stale_revision`. For affordances with `expect: boundary`.

expectation.description: What an invoke is conditional on. A form that does not match the affordance's `expect` fails with `invalid_arguments`.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

columns.description: The column header: the keys rows' `columns` use, with their captions.

total.description: How many rows the list holds; read more with `bn.interaction.choices`.

offset.description: The index of the first of `rows`. Absent: 0.

selection.description: How many rows the player picks: none, one, several, or a count of each.

activate.description: The affordance that picks a row (`args.row`).

filterable.description: The list takes a filter text: invoking the filter affordance among `affordances` opens a prompt whose text narrows `rows`. Absent: it does not.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

unread.description: Something in the tab is new to the player.

select.description: The affordance that switches tab (`args.row` = tab id).

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

relation.description: `peers`: parts of equal standing. `detail`: the later parts describe the first.

active.description: The child the player's input goes to.

split.description: Parts shown together, in reading order. Layout is the client's.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

max.description: What the value can reach. Absent: unbounded.

tone.description: Whether the value is good or bad news, such as over capacity.

stats.description: Facts about the pane, such as what it holds against what it can hold.

filter.description: The filter the pane applies, as typed. Absent: none.

panel.description: A titled pane with one child.

value.description: The current value, in the form `fill` takes.

options.description: The values a `select` field takes, by id.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

submit.description: The affordance that sends the fields.

form.description: Values the player types or sets.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

tone.description: Whether the native screen marks the text as good or bad news.

role.description: `terminal_output`: what an in-game computer or console prints. `banner`: the game's title art and version over the main menu.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

grid.description: Cells placed on a grid of `cols` by `rows`, counted from the top-left.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

mode.description: `world`: the streamed map (`bn.snapshot.part`, `bn.events`) with this overlay. `overmap`: the overmap squares in `overmap`, with the cursor in `target`.

map.description: The map, with the cursor or target the screen is choosing.

affordances.description: Ids of `screen.affordances` that act on this component.

canvas_component.description: A native window as drawn, such as a software mini-game: one list of runs per row, each run [text, foreground, background] over cells that share their colors, with curses color indexes 0-15 as in the overmap. Blank cells that end a row are left out.

component.description: A generic component, by `kind`. Clients render every kind without knowing the screen.

id.description: The horizontal part (north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest, center for none), then _above or _below; straight up and down are above and below.

name.description: The name the native game gives the direction, in the connection's language.

heading.description: A direction as the native game names it.

id.description: The layout in use (classic, labels, ...), as the native panel options name it.

side.description: The side of the screen the native sidebar sits on (the SIDEBAR_POSITION option).

id.description: The panel manager's name for the panel, untranslated.

label.description: The name the native panel options print, translated.

enabled.description: The player has not switched the panel off in the native panel options.

height.description: Rows. Absent for the panel that takes the rest of the column.

panels.description: In the panel manager's order, top to bottom. Panels the native panel options do not list in this state (the vehicle panel outside a vehicle) are left out.

sidebar_layout.description: The native sidebar options. A change the player makes in the native panel options is published with the next avatar.

label.description: The heading the native compass panel prints for it (North:, NE:), translated. Absent for center, which it does not print.

id.description: The entity id of the creature.

distance.description: Squares from the avatar, as the native sound and safe mode code count them.

compass_direction.description: The creatures the native compass panel lists toward one direction.
